text: Flat two-colour production artwork for vectorisation, on a plain pure white background, in a tall narrow vertical frame. Subject: a fish and a lamb meeting in a kiss, stacked vertically and filling the height of the frame. In the upper half, a large fish like a salmon dives head down: its body curves in a big C, the wide forked tail fanning up at the top right, the back arching to the left with the dorsal fin, two pectoral fins, a row of small oval spots along the back, a curved gill line, and the head pointing down at the centre. In the lower half, a young lamb rears up on its hind legs, seen from the side, its head raised straight up so that the tip of its nose touches the fish's closed mouth; one front leg is lifted high to the right with the hoof up, the other bent against its chest, the body sloping down to the left, a short curly tail at the left, the hind legs bent and kicking at the bottom, the ears held back horizontally. Drawing style: bold cut-paper and linocut silhouettes, sharp and confident, with a few thick white cut lines inside the shapes for the fins, the spots, the gill, the scalloped fleece curls and the hooves. Strong, dynamic, elegant, like a contemporary woodcut. Colours: the fish is one single flat solid colour, pure blue #1F4FBF; the lamb is one single flat solid colour, pure green #1E9E5A; every inner line is white. No gradient, no texture, no shadow, no outline of another colour, no paper, no card, no frame: only white, blue and green. Both eyes are drawn like real animal eyes, as in a natural history engraving, never like a human or cartoon eye: no white highlight dot, no round iris ring, no eyelashes, no eyebrows. Faces calm and neutral, mouths closed, no teeth. The fish's eye is one small solid round dot, cut out in white, with no highlight; its mouth is a long natural closed line following the jaw from the tip of the snout, touching the lamb's nose. The lamb's eye is a real sheep's eye set on the side of the head: a narrow horizontal almond outline with a heavy upper eyelid and a horizontal slit pupil, looking up at the fish.
